easy.def: Just right, with no mistake.
examples: It fits exactly.
That is exactly right.
She knew exactly what to do.

more.def: In a way that is completely correct, with nothing more or less.
examples: The two pieces fit together exactly.
It is exactly three o'clock.
I knew exactly where I had put my keys.

easy.def: To look at something very closely.
examples: The doctor will examine my ear.
I examine the bug with my eyes.
The vet examines our dog.

more.def: To look at or check something carefully to learn more about it.
examples: We examined the leaf under a magnifying glass.
The detective examined the room for clues.
She examined the coin closely to read its date.

easy.def: One thing that shows what others are like.
examples: Give me an example.
A dog is an example of a pet.
This is a good example.

more.def: One thing that shows what a group of things is like.
examples: A cat is an example of a pet.
Can you give an example of a mammal?
The teacher showed an example of a good story.

easy.def: Very, very good.
examples: You did an excellent job.
The food was excellent.
She is an excellent swimmer.

more.def: Extremely good; better than most.
examples: You did an excellent job on your project.
The restaurant has excellent soup.
He is an excellent chess player.

easy.def: But not.
examples: Everyone came except Sam.
I like all fruit except pears.
The store is open every day except Sunday.

more.def: Not including; leaving out.
examples: Everyone in the class went on the trip except Jo, who was sick.
All of the animals, except the lions, were awake.
The library is open every day except Sunday.

easy.def: Very happy and full of energy.
examples: I am excited for my birthday.
The kids were excited.
She felt excited.

more.def: Feeling very happy and eager about something.
examples: We were excited about the trip to the zoo.
The excited puppy wagged its tail.
She was excited to start school.

easy.def: Making you feel very happy and eager.
examples: The game was exciting.
An exciting day.
What an exciting story!

more.def: Causing strong feelings of interest or joy.
examples: The last minute of the game was exciting.
We went on an exciting trip.
She read an exciting story about a pirate.

easy.def: To say it is okay that someone did something.
examples: Please excuse me.
He excused her.
Excuse my mess.

more.def: To forgive a small mistake, or to let someone leave.
examples: Please excuse me for being late to class.
The teacher excused the students for lunch.
She excused his mistake because it was an accident.

easy.def: A reason you give for something you did.
examples: I have an excuse.
His excuse was silly.
That is not a good excuse.

more.def: A reason that you give to explain why something happened or was not done.
examples: His excuse for being late was that the bus broke down.
She had no excuse for forgetting her homework.
Rain is not an excuse to stay inside all day.

easy.def: Very, very tired.
examples: I was exhausted after the long walk.
The exhausted baby fell asleep.
We were exhausted after the swim.

more.def: Extremely tired, with no energy left.
examples: After the race, the exhausted runners lay down on the grass.
The exhausted hikers finally reached their camp.
I was exhausted from staying up too late.

easy.def: To be real.
examples: Dinosaurs existed long ago.
Dragons do not exist.
Unicorns do not exist.

more.def: To be real, or to be alive.
examples: Dinosaurs existed millions of years ago.
Dragons do not exist outside of stories.
Life exists on Earth.

easy.def: To think something will happen.
examples: I expect it will rain.
We expect Grandma at noon.
She expected a gift.

more.def: To believe that something will happen or that someone will arrive.
examples: We expect the first snow to fall sometime next week.
The teacher expects everyone to bring a pencil.
I was expecting a letter, but nothing came today.

easy.def: Something that happens to you.
examples: The trip was a fun experience.
Camping was a new experience.
It was a scary experience.

more.def: Something you do or that happens to you.
examples: Riding a horse was a new experience for me.
The trip to the cave was an exciting experience.
She shared the experience with her friends.

easy.def: What you know from doing something.
examples: She has experience with horses.
A guide with experience led us.
Experience helps you do better.

more.def: Knowledge or skill that you get from doing something for a long time.
examples: The guide had years of experience climbing mountains.
Experience taught him to check the weather before hiking.
You need experience to fly a plane.

easy.def: A test to find out something.
examples: We did an experiment with ice and salt.
In our experiment, the egg floated.
The experiment made bubbles.

more.def: A careful test done to discover or prove something.
examples: Our science experiment showed that plants grow toward light.
The scientist repeated the experiment to check her results.
As an experiment, we tried baking the bread without sugar.

easy.def: A person who knows a lot about something.
examples: He is a bird expert.
The expert fixed it.
She is a math expert.

more.def: A person who has special skill or knows a lot about a subject.
examples: The bird expert identified the song.
An expert fixed the broken clock.
She is an expert at chess.

easy.def: To tell how or why.
examples: Please explain the game.
She explained the rules.
He explains how it works.

more.def: To make something clear by giving details or reasons.
examples: The teacher explained how plants make food from sunlight.
Can you explain why the sky is blue?
She explained the rules of the game to the new player.

easy.def: To look around a new place.
examples: Let's explore the garden!
We explore the beach for shells.
The cat explores the new house.

more.def: To travel through or look carefully at a place to learn about it.
examples: The divers explored a cave deep under the sea.
Robots explore the surface of Mars.
On vacation, we explored the old part of the city.

easy.def: No longer living anywhere on Earth.
examples: Dinosaurs are extinct.
Some animals may go extinct.
The extinct bird had a big beak.

more.def: No longer existing; having no living members left.
examples: The dodo bird became extinct hundreds of years ago.
Woolly mammoths have been extinct for thousands of years.
People are working to keep tigers from becoming extinct.

easy.def: More than usual.
examples: I need an extra pencil.
We have extra time.
Take an extra cookie.

more.def: More than what is usual or needed.
examples: Bring an extra sweater in case it gets cold.
We had extra time before the bus came.
Add an extra spoon of sugar.
